subject: Clarifying CCPA/CPRA role and telemetry aggregation — delegated handling question
messages:
From: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@healthpay.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: privacy@healthpay.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification: telemetry aggregation + service provider vs controller

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. A quick set of follow-ups from our legal/privacy team as we map Redwood into our DPA and state annex:

1) Role clarity: HealthPay needs an explicit statement that Redwood will act as a "Service Provider" (CCPA/CPRA definition) for telemetry and for inference outputs derived from customer-provided data. Can you confirm the language you expect to obligate Redwood to the limited-use/service-provider restrictions?

2) Telemetry aggregation: we collect high-volume usage telemetry (latency, token counts, model selection signals). We typically treat aggregated telemetry as not a "sale" if it’s non-identifiable. Can you confirm whether Redwood considers rolled-up model-usage aggregates (e.g., daily model token counts, per-customer error rates where identifiers are hashed) to fall outside the "sale" definition? We need that for our state privacy annex.

3) Subprocessors/onshore fallback: given regulatory requirements, we need a documented onshore fallback plan and a list of subprocessors that will process unredacted logs or telemetry. Please attach your current subprocessor roster and proposed onshore fallback commitments (SLA/response windows).

I attached a short telemetry matrix our team uses — feel free to annotate. Looking to close these items for our procurement review next week.

—Jacob
Jacob Reed
Sr. Manager, Vendor Privacy
HealthPay

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@healthpay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: telemetry aggregation + service provider vs controller

Jacob — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I’ve looped in Karthik (infra) for a short technical note and Marissa (legal) for suggested DPA wording. I’ve also attached our draft redlines to our standard DPA for reference.

Quick answers:
- Role: Redwood accepts the role of "Service Provider" for customer-provided data and inference outputs produced from that data. We will add explicit limited-use language in the DPA/US annex.
- Telemetry aggregation: our typical practice is to classify aggregated telemetry (non-invertible counts/metrics) as operational/usage analytics and not a "sale." There are a few nuances (described below) we should align on.
- Subprocessors & onshore fallback: attached is our current subprocessor roster and our onshore fallback playbook summary. We can commit to an onshore fallback for telemetry investigations and for audit evidence within a mutually agreed SLA; suggest a 48–72 hour window for critical log access.

I’ll let Karthik answer the telemetry technicalities in-line. Marissa — could you propose the explicit clause we should include in the US privacy annex that mirrors the SP/limited-use language HealthPay needs?

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@healthpay.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 12:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: telemetry aggregation + service provider vs controller

Hi Jacob,
Couple of technical clarifications on telemetry so folks can assess re: "sale":

1) Aggregation method: when we report daily model token counts per customer we use a one-way HMAC key that is scoped per-customer in our metrics pipeline. That means raw identifiers are not present in the aggregated store.
2) Derived metrics: per-customer error rates are computed in a transient pipeline; the computed metric is stored without original inputs. We retain raw request logs only in a short-lived buffer (up to 7 days) for debugging and fraud detection; after that the raw logs are purged or moved to encrypted cold storage with restricted access.
3) Access controls: access to unredacted logs is role-based and requires an audited justification plus approval from our security team. For onshore fallback, we can replicate the relevant ephemeral logs to an onshore-only S3 bucket under HealthPay's AO (access-only) role for investigations.

Caveats: if HealthPay requires that aggregated metrics never include any customer UID even temporarily in any intermediate store we can add that as a contractual control but it will change some debugging timelines. Happy to diagram the pipeline for your team.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infra & Reliability

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@healthpay.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: telemetry aggregation + service provider vs controller

Jacob,

Thanks for raising these. Draft legal language suggestions attached (Redwood_DPA_draft_redlines_v1.pdf). Key items we propose to include in the US annex:
- Explicit "Service Provider" designation for customer-provided personal data and for inference outputs derived from that data.
- Limited-use restriction: Redwood will not sell, share, or otherwise disclose personal information for purposes outside the service-provider relationship; analytics/telemetry will be scoped to non-identifiable aggregates.
- Telemetry definition: define "aggregated telemetry" as metrics that cannot reasonably be re-identified to a natural person or household and exclude transient debugging logs from that definition.
- Subprocessor/onshore fallback: Redwood will provide a current subprocessor list and 30-day notice for additions. For regulated customers, Redwood will provide an onshore fallback replication option with confirmation within 48–72 hours for critical log access and a quarterly attestation of access controls.

Questions for HealthPay: are you comfortable with the 48–72 hour onshore access window and the HMAC-based aggregation method as described? If HealthPay requires stricter constraints (e.g., no intermediate store with any identifier), we can propose a narrow amendment but would like to track the operational impact.

—Marissa Cole
General Counsel (acting)
Redwood Inference

From: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@healthpay.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: telemetry aggregation + service provider vs controller

Marissa, Grace, Karthik — thanks for the quick responses and the redlines. HealthPay legal has two follow-ups:

- The 48–72 hour onshore access window is acceptable subject to a SLAT commitment in the annex; can Redwood propose minimal SLA language (uptime/response window + escalation contact)?
- On telemetry: the HMAC approach sounds reasonable. We will want the telemetry definition in the annex to explicitly exclude transient debugging buffers from the "aggregated telemetry" category (so debug logs may be treated as restricted). Please add that granular definition in redlines and we’ll review.

We should be able to close this on Monday after you push the two small changes.

Appreciate the speedy turnaround — I’ll attach any additional procurement notes if needed.

—Jacob
